title.narrative: Suva-Nausori Water Supply and Sewerage Project (Supplementary Loan)

description.narrative: The objective of the project is to assist human and economic development in Fiji through the development of water supply and sewerage services in the Suva and Nausori urban areas. A new water source will be developed, water treatment plants will be extended and rehabilitated, and pipelines and distribution systems will be developed; sewerage pumping stations and trunk services will be rehabilitated, and sewerage networks will be extended. The project will provide water and sewerage services of a standard that is suitable for commercialized operations, and will complement institutional developments that are being assisted by the Bank.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Increased coverage and improved delivery of water supply and sewerage services to the residents of the Suva Nausori area.

Access to sewerage service increases from 110,000 (base year 2005) to 140,000 by 2013 Progress/Status: Commissioning of the Sambula North and the Suva Point sewer network will increase the access. Data Source: WSD and WAF monthly monitoring data and annual reports. Actual value:

Uncontrolled overflows from the sewer network decreases from more than1,200 per year (base year 2008) to less than 500 by 2013 Data Source: WSD and WAF monthly monitoring data and annual reports. Actual value:

Number of unplanned water service interruptions decreases from more than 2,000 per year (base year 2005) to less than 800 by 2013 Progress/Status: Same as above for all the indicators. Data Source: WSD and WAF monthly monitoring data and annual reports. Actual value:

Reduction in unaccounted for water from 55% of water produced (base year 2005 to 30% by 2013 Progress/Status: Reduced to approximately 45% by 2012. Data Source: WSD and WAF monthly monitoring data and annual reports. Actual value:

Access to water services increases from 97% (base year 2005) to 99% of the Suva-Nausori population by 2013 Progress/Status: Part of the project has been completed through the original loan L2055 in September 2012. . Physical works financed by the Supplementary loan L2603 will be completed in 2013. Full impacts and outcomes assessment will be done on full completion as part of the EA's PCR. Data Source: WSD and WAF monthly monitoring data and annual reports. Actual value:

100% of samples extracted from the regional water supply network meet World Health Organization guidelines by 2013 (baseline: 99% in 2005) Data Source: Quarterly and annual National Water Quality Laboratory reports Actual value:
